static_traits.name: Zhang Chen
static_traits.medical_history: No notable physical illness; no psychotherapy history; no similar problems occurred before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, organized thinking, able to self-reflect and actively cooperate; neutral tone, able to identify and describe their own thoughts and feelings

basic_info.main_problem: I always feel disappointed when watching my favorite TV show The Walking Dead; this feeling has gradually worsened over the past six months, to the point where I expect to be disappointed before each episode begins, affecting my enjoyment of the show.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize that the constant expectation of disappointment is taking away my enjoyment of watching 'The Walking Dead', and I hope to enjoy the show again and reduce the influence of negative thoughts.

core_beliefs: Beautiful things will ultimately disappoint me

special_situations.event: Before sitting down to watch an episode of The Walking Dead
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an episode does not meet my expectations, I will be disappointed; to avoid a bigger letdown, I need to prepare myself mentally in advance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Before watching, presets 'I will be disappointed' as self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This episode definitely will not be good; it will disappoint me

special_situations.event: Noticing small flaws or details that are not to one's liking while watching
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a flaw appears, it means the whole episode is not worthwhile or not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Being picky and magnifying shortcomings, ignoring merits
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These problems prove this episode is bad

special_situations.event: After finishing watching, evaluating the whole episode
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One bad experience can prove my overall judgment is correct and foretells that it will be the same afterward
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using 'see, I knew it' to confirm and consolidate the original negative evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: See, I knew this episode would not be good

special_situations.event: Over the past six months, raised expectations for the plot direction and paid more critical attention to what might go wrong
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Series episodes should meet my high and specific expectations, otherwise it counts as failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting high standards and judging each episode by them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If it does not develop as I expect, this episode is terrible

positive_force: Still having love for and motivation to engage with the show
Willing to seek help and accept suggestions for cognitive restructuring
Able to identify and describe one's own automatic thoughts
Having a close friend one can confide in (potential support resource)
negative_force: Continually making negative predictions before watching (expecting to be disappointed)
Focusing excessively on flaws, ignoring positive segments
Disqualifying positive experiences and generalizing from a single poor experience to the whole
Raised and rigid expectations lead to harsher judgment
Has not shared this difficulty with friends; lacks correction from an outside perspective

target_behavior.behavior: Persistently experiences disappointment and negative expectations before and after watching The Walking Dead, and nitpicks during viewing
antecedent: Sitting down to prepare to watch a TV series
Before starting, thinks 'this episode may not be good'
Holds higher and more specific expectations for the plot direction and attends to what might go wrong
target_behavior.core_reason: Anticipatory disappointment driven by cognitive biases (fortune telling, mental filtering, disqualifying the positive, overgeneralization, all-or-nothing thinking), causing the client to selectively attend to negative cues while watching
target_behavior.function: Engages in psychological self-protection by presupposing disappointment and picking faults, attempting to reduce the sense of letdown and maintain a subjective sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Enjoyment of watching dramas markedly declines, mood is affected, and overall enjoyment of the activity decreases
